ca_two_mile_bar.blurb: Two Mile Bar is a short andesite bluff, roughly 30 feet tall, among the crags strung along the Highway 108 corridor in the Sierra foothills. Nearly everything here is traditional, with a single top-rope line, and the grades run from 5.8 to 5.12 with most climbs in the 5.10 and 5.11 range and a few moderates to start on. Cracks make up much of the menu, and trees along the rim give easy anchors for rope work. The rim is loose and strewn with boulders, so take care up there, and poison oak grows in the area. Expect a 15 to 25 minute uphill hike on a worn cattle path, then an easy walk-off back down.

ca_twin_crags.blurb: Twin Crags is a cliff of columnar basalt about a mile north of Tahoe City, looking out over the Truckee River toward Lake Tahoe. Almost all of the 19 climbs are trad, plus one sport route and one top-rope line, ranging from 5.7 to 5.12 with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. Many lines blend bolts with gear placements, and bolts can be far apart. The rock gets blockier and looser toward the top, though it often climbs more pleasantly than it appears from below. The wall faces south to southwest, which makes it a handy choice on cooler days, and it tends to be quieter than the bigger Tahoe crags.
ca_twin_crags.approach: A trail leaves from the end of the road and reaches the crag in about 10 minutes.

ca_toxic_avenger_area.blurb: Toxic Avenger Area is a bouldering zone on the West Rim of the Happy Boulders near Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra. Its 19 problems cover a wide range, from about V2 to V12, with the weight of them between V3 and V11, so it suits stronger boulderers more than beginners. The style is steep pocket pulling, and the best-known problem here is a crimpy test piece. The zone is shaded all day, and the West Rim as a whole feels cooler and less busy than the middle of the canyon. It sits just uphill of Safesurfer and Froz; walk up the trail from Froz, or come in from the Desert Skies side.

ca_stirrup_towers.blurb: Stirrup Towers is a run of small crags on the eastern side of Joshua Tree National Park, in the Pinto Basin near Stirrup Tank. The formations stretch northwest to southeast over a few hundred yards. Most of the 18 climbs are trad, with a few top-rope and bolted lines, graded from 5.6 to 5.10, so it works well for moderate leaders, with most climbs between 5.8 and 5.10. Rock quality is fair to decent, though the wider area varies from poor to good. It is a calmer alternative to the busy Hidden Valley side of the park.
ca_stirrup_towers.approach: Walk east from the Stirrup Tank parking area to reach the north end of the towers.

ca_cockroach_crag.blurb: Cockroach Crag is a small, squat brown outcrop in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park. Of its 18 climbs, almost all are trad and two are top-rope, with grades from 5.5 to 5.11: about a third are easy to moderate, a handful sit at 5.8 and 5.9, and the rest are 5.10 and 5.11. The rock is loose and the holds can pull off, so test everything, but the climbing is still fun, especially as a second. Every line can be top-roped by walking up the gully on either side. Check the rock beside it too, since a famous hand crack lives next door rather than on this crag.
